text:
vivian: FYI EU2 GPU pool can't finish onboarding. Kubelets failing to pull secrets after the firewall default-deny deploy at ~09:58. KMS 403s.
marcus: Which key / error?
vivian: From /var/log/keystore on gpu-eu2-ctl-3:
```
2026-03-23T10:01:03Z ERROR keystore: AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on arn:aws:kms:eu-west-2:111:key/abcd-1234
```
vivian: Keystore talks to our KMS grant broker over a privatelink endpoint. The endpoint policy was tightened in the firewall change.
ops-bot: alert: keystore.kms.decrypt denied 403 x38 in 5m — https://ops/redwood/alerts/keystore-kms-403
ben: Looks like the new endpoint policy included a deny that matched the privatelink role/principal. That shadowed the earlier allow for keystore.
kyra: We rolled the deny to close a broad audit egress hole (wanted only shipper-bucket access). Did we forget to whitelist keystore-privatelink role explicitly?
ben: Confirmed no whitelist. The deny statement was too greedy.
marcus: Mitigation? We have a production rollout relying on these GPUs later today.
oncall-sre: Two quick paths: 1) rollback endpoint policy (fast but undoes audit hardening), 2) create a narrowly scoped KMS grant + patch endpoint policy to explicitly allow the keystore principal. Option 2 is preferred.
kyra: Agreed — do option 2 first. If it fails, rollback. Approving emergency grant for short TTL.
vivian: Proposed grant CLI:
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/keystore-eu2 \
  --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111:role/keystore-privatelink \
  --operations Decrypt \
  --name "eu2-temp-onboard"
```
vivian: And minimal endpoint change: add a single Allow statement for keystore role to call kms:Decrypt/s3:GetObject for keystore paths.
ben: I'll prepare vpce policy file and set a 4h TTL on the grant. Handing to infra for deploy as a canary to eu2-edge-az1.
marcus: Also, watch audit shipper metrics — we might have matched shipper traffic depending on how the policy was written.
kyra: Shipper path was intended to remain allowed; the deny accidentally hit the privatelink principal. After we patch, validate kinesis/s3 delivery, but likely fine.
oncall-sre: I'll add a synthetic that calls keystore.Decrypt and checks node readiness. Escalate to rollback if >30 nodes failing after 10m.
ops-bot: deploy request created by ben — https://deploy/redwood/1234
vivian: Creating grant now.
vivian: Grant created id g-0xbeefcafe. Testing on a single canary node.
vivian: Canary node decrypted secrets and joined. kubelet Ready. :tada:
ben: Patching endpoint policy and applying in eu2-edge-az1. Grant TTL set to 4h.
marcus: Quick cost note — adding a regional audit mirror to avoid cross-region egress could run ~€120-160/day in S3 storage+requests. Raising for product/cost visibility.
kyra: Put that as a TODO in the audit-hardening PR. Prefer retention vs risky tight denies.
oncall-sre: Monitoring started 10:40. Current status: 13/16 previously pending nodes recovered after grant+policy patch. Continuing to watch.
vivian: I'll draft a short postmortem and include a minimal policy snippet for keystore so this doesn't regress.
ben: I'll also add an automated test in the privatelink CI that validates keystore/grants aren't blocked by deny statements.
marcus: Nice work. Thanks all.
ops-bot: alert still open — human to close after full recovery — https://ops/redwood/alerts/keystore-kms-403
